pages.text: In the meadow beyond the backyard fence lived an Elephant, very big and very strong. When a log fell across the stream, Elephant moved it. "Being big is for helping," he liked to say.
One morning, a tiny seed blew into the curl of his trunk — and stuck. Oh, it itched!
Elephant shook his trunk — shake, shake, shake. The seed stayed. He blew his biggest blow — whoooosh! The seed stayed.
He stomped his great gray feet — STOMP, STOMP, STOMP! The seed stayed. "I am big and strong," he sighed, "but I cannot fix one tiny seed."
"Excuse me," said a small voice. On a blade of grass sat a Ladybug, red as a berry. "I could get it out. I'm just the right small."
Elephant almost said, You're too little. Instead, he said, "Yes, please."
Ladybug walked up his trunk on tiny, tickly feet — tip, tip, tip — and rolled the seed out like a crumb. "Ahhh," said Elephant. It was the best ahhh of his whole life.
No one is too small to help — and no one is too big to ask.
Y colorín colorado, este cuento se ha acabado.

vocab.kidDefinition: a big open field of soft grass and flowers
an elephant's long, bendy nose that can grab and hold things
when a soft touch makes you giggle and squirm
let out one big slow breath when you feel tired or stuck
